summary.headline: Midwest H1 FY27 revenue up 24% and PAT up 18% YoY; quartz turned EBIT positive in Q2 with volumes at ~16,000 tons.
summary.overview: Management reported H1 FY27 revenue growth of 24% and PAT growth of about 17-18% YoY, with Q2 revenue up about 15% and PAT up about 9% YoY. Quartz business reached EBIT breakeven/positive in Q2 on about 16,000 tons volume, while Q2 margins were flat QoQ due to quartz under-absorption and a 30-35% rise in fuel costs (about 6% margin impact, passed on to customers). Operating cash flow was negative in H1 on receivables, inventory build and trade payable settlements; working capital cycle rose to 127 days from 104 days in FY26. Rare earth projects (Sri Lanka, Indonesia, KMML) remain pre-commercial, with permissions and definitive agreements slipping into next quarter.

segments.name: Granite (natural stone)
segments.commentary: H1 volume growth about 14%, Q2 volume growth about 7%. Management guides FY27 granite volume growth of 10-12% plus 3-4% price/currency, for 14-15% revenue growth. Export realisations about INR88,000/cubic metre for Galaxy and INR39,000-40,000 for Black (Black export about INR1 lakh).

segments.name: Quartz (engineered stone / solar-grade)
segments.commentary: Q2 volume about 16,000 tons; September about 9,000 tons. Realisation about INR8,500-9,500/ton; FY27 quartz revenue now guided at about INR90 crore (earlier INR100-120 crore). Quartz turned EBIT positive in Q2 and targets full-year standalone PAT profit.

segments.name: Rare earths / mineral sands
segments.commentary: Pre-revenue. Sri Lanka targeted as first commercial project, permissions expected this quarter with work next quarter; Indonesia (via Singapore subsidiary, Perminas) definitive agreement targeted this quarter; KMML awaiting new Kerala government administrative team.

guidance_outlook: Q3 FY27 quartz volume guided at 25,000-30,000 tons and Q4 at 35,000-40,000 tons; monthly run rate about 9,000 tons, target above 10,000 tons next month.
Q3 described as a normal quarter with no downtrend; Q4 expected to be the heaviest quarter. Management expects no major cyclone impact going forward.
FY27 quartz revenue framed at about INR90 crore on a comfort basis; INR100 crore if 15,000 tons is reached by early January.
Next year (FY28) quartz volume target about double FY27, ramping to 18,000 tons per month consistently.
Medium-term (3-4 years) targets: 2.5x revenue, 3x profitability, 35% ROCE, backed by INR300 crore capex.
Electric truck fleet to be fully converted within 24 months; annual savings INR4-5 crore from 10 trucks plus 6 MW captive solar.
capex_capacity: Quartz Phase 2 expansion will double processing capacity to 606,000 MTPA; first phase (regular solar/engineered stone) by Q2 FY28, high-purity quartz (HPQ) by Q3/Q4 FY28.
About INR120 crore of Phase 2 capex to be spent over the next four quarters.
Of the INR300 crore total capex, the majority is for rare earth mineral separation and consolidation plants (Sri Lanka); INR120 crore is for quartz Phase 2.
Three new APMDC granite mine LOIs (one Black Granite, two in Chittur, two in Srikakulam) on raising-cum-sale contract basis with low upfront investment.
1 MW solar plant under installation, due to complete this financial year; 6 MW captive solar tied up.
demand_pricing: Engineered stone realisation grades range from INR9,500 to INR14,500/ton; blended quartz realisation about INR9,500-9,600/ton.
Fuel cost up 30-35% YoY in H1 (from about INR90 to INR120-130 per unit), with about 6% margin impact fully passed on through pricing; export realisation also rose about 4% on currency.

Quartz customers include Triveni (solar glass, supplies to be fully met this year; Triveni doubling capacity), Gold Plus in Bellary (second customer starting Q2), and Margal in Karnataka; engineered stone manufacturers such as Pokarna and Marudhar are named potential customers.
Management says a US oil-tariff concern led to positioning in Thailand, Vietnam and Europe; no shipment impact so far, with exports to ramp beyond 15,000 tons per month.
Rare earth oxide premium pricing expected to persist per management, citing non-China supply gaps and magnet demand growth of 12-13% per year.

qa_highlights.question: Quartz volume for the quarter and current monthly run rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Q2 quartz volume about 16,000 tons; last month about 9,000 tons, targeting above 10,000 tons next month and 12,000-15,000 tons per month next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Why was operating cash flow negative in H1?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO cited about INR25 crore extra receivables from extended domestic credit after GST cut, INR14-15 crore inventory build, and about INR20 crore trade payable settlements.

qa_highlights.question: What caused the Rajasthan... mine ban-type issue and its impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is a rectification of a high-wall issue at a Galaxy mine, not a ban; work started 3 weeks earlier, expected 5-6 weeks to resolve, with production shifted to a neighbouring mine and no major impact expected.

qa_highlights.question: Status of rare earth projects (KMML, Indonesia, Sri Lanka)?
qa_highlights.answer: KMML awaits a new Kerala government administrative team; Indonesia definitive agreement targeted this quarter with ground work next quarter; Sri Lanka permissions expected this quarter with work starting next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Granite and quartz volume and revenue outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Granite volume growth guided at 10-12% plus 3-4% price for 14-15% revenue growth; Q3 and Q4 to be stronger than Q1-Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital cycle rise to 127 days?
qa_highlights.answer: Driven by a new APMDC JV with no bill discounting limit, domestic credit extension and inventory; management says no further domestic credit extension and expects the cycle to ease.

risks_watch: Quartz margin: Q2 margins flat QoQ; quartz under-absorption must reverse as volumes reach 25,000-40,000 tons in Q3-Q4 to hit guided profitability.
Working capital: cycle at 127 days and negative H1 operating cash flow; watch receivables and whether the cycle eases from Q3.
Rare earth timelines depend on government approvals (Sri Lanka permissions, KMML team, Kerala government) and Indonesia definitive agreement, all slated for this quarter.
Fuel cost and monsoon/cyclone exposure; pass-through of fuel costs assumed to hold through pricing.
Quartz FY27 revenue guidance cut to about INR90 crore from INR100-120 crore; volume ramp needs to reach 15,000 tons by early January.
summary.management_tone: Confident on long-term targets and quartz ramp, but notably hedged on near-term timelines: rare earth approvals and KMML are framed as outside management's control, and quartz volume was tracked well below the earlier 20,000-ton Q2 expectation.
key_quotes: I'm also happy to share that our quartz business has become EBIT positive.
For the next 3-4 years, our aim to achieve 2.5x revenue growth, 3x profitability, and 35% ROCE is firm and backed by capex of INR300 crores.
So I think you can factor in around INR90 crores for this year on a comfort basis.
So the entire hit that we had because of the fuel increase, the cost increase from INR90 all the way to INR120, INR130 also, the 40% increase in fuel is completely passed on to the customers.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q2 margins were flat QoQ (consolidated PAT margin 16.37) with quartz under-absorption, and the 30-35% fuel cost rise (about 6% margin impact) is passed through; quartz must reach 25,000-40,000 tons in Q3-Q4 for operating leverage to show.

rows.label: Volume growth

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is not disclosed and the INR300 crore capex plan (mostly rare earth separation and consolidation) is already set, so a new quartz capex decision depends on the Phase 2 ramp and the 15,000-ton target.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Quartz volume tracked well below the earlier 20,000-ton Q2 expectation, the run rate is about 9,000 t/month against a 25,000-30,000 t Q3 guide, and rare earth timelines depend on government approvals.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: High-purity quartz (HPQ) line from Phase 2 is under construction with commissioning targeted Q3/Q4 FY28; exports are ramping to beyond 15,000 t/month.

rows.label: Quartz customer ramp (Triveni, Gold Plus, Margal)

rows.label: Working capital cycle easing from 127 days

rows.label: Rare earth approvals (Sri Lanka, Indonesia, KMML)
rows.why: Sri Lanka permissions, the Indonesia definitive agreement and the KMML Kerala team are all slated for this quarter, but the projects are pre-revenue and approval slippage is already visible.

oneOffs.what: Fuel cost up 30-35% YoY in H1 (about 6% margin impact), passed fully to customers; price pass-through lifts revenue but not recurring profit growth
Export realisation up about 4% on currency in H1, a price tailwind rather than volume

quality.why: Q2 granite volume grew about 7% YoY (H1 about 14%) with pricing and currency adding a few points, and quartz only just reached EBIT positive on about 16,000 tons, so the growth is mainly recurring. Q2 revenue was up about 15% and PAT about 9%, and price pass-through and a weaker-currency export tailwind help the top line, while the brief gives no clearly one-off gain or base effect.
